transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-18
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 43 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alec Moreno (Redwood AE), Marisol Gomez (Redwood SE), Rashid Khan (Redwood SE), Ethan Park (Talon Head of Platform), Lena Ortiz (Talon Security Lead), Jonas Reed (CTO), Priya Mahajan (SRE)

Auto-generated summary (auto):
Talon Ventures is evaluating Redwood for a mixture of hosted and private deployment. Primary concerns: SOC two / ISO alignment, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC and fine-grained audit logs, KMS integration and HSM usage, data retention and e-discovery. They want a benchmark in a private VPC and clear documentation on encryption and log exports prior to a pilot.

Topics covered:
- Compliance posture (SOC2/ISO) and artifacts
- Authentication and provisioning: SSO, SAML, SCIM, RBAC
- Key management: KMS/HSM support, BYOK and rotation
- Auditability: request/response logging, retention windows, export formats
- Hosting choices: Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved pools vs Private (VPC)
- Next steps and pilot gating criteria

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alec Moreno: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, I'm Alec on AE side and with me is Marisol and Rashid from engineering. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Jonas Reed: Good, thanks. busy week but we're excited to dig in.
[00:12] Ethan Park: Yeah thanks. want to make sure we get into the security detail — Lena has the list.
[00:17] Lena Ortiz: Hi. yes I'll try to keep it tight — main asks: SOC two artifacts, SAML + SCIM provisioning, RBAC model, audit logs format and retention options, and KMS integration. also curious about private deployment timeline.
[00:29] Marisol Gomez: Perfect — we'll walk through each, maybe start with compliance and then move into auth and keys, then hosting. sound OK?
[00:34] Lena Ortiz: Yep.

[01:02] Marisol Gomez: So on SOC two we are a SOC 2 environment — we maintain a SOC 2 attestation and have a controls matrix. we also map to ISO27001 controls; we typically deliver a summary package for sales intake and on enterprise contracts we can provide our latest SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. sorry, type two.
[01:22] Ethan Park: when you say "summary package", what does that include? list of controls? encryption specifics?
[01:27] Marisol Gomez: it includes scope, auditor, period covered, and a controls mapping — logical access, encryption in transit/at rest, incident response, change management. we do not include customer-specific logs in that artifact. for more detailed questions we point to our security docs and can run a security questionnaire.
[01:45] Lena Ortiz: Do you have any attestations for data residency or EU-specific controls? our workloads will have EU residency requirements.
[01:51] Alec Moreno: Yes — we have regions in eu-west and can set tenancy in those regions. SOC two is global; for EU-specific we provide data processing addendums and we can discuss contractual residency language for Private deployments.

[03:10] Jonas Reed: For onboarding we need federation + provisioning. our IdP supports SAML 2.0 and SCIM for groups. how does Redwood integrate?
[03:18] Rashid Khan: We support SAML for SSO and SCIM for provisioning groups and users in our console for Dedicated and Hosted. for Private deployments the control plane supports SAML and SCIM, but provisioning can be routed to the customer's IdP via SCIM bridge if they require on-prem provisioning.
[03:35] Lena Ortiz: any gotchas around session length and session revocation? we need to be able to revoke sessions quickly when an engineer leaves.
[03:41] Marisol Gomez: session tokens respect IdP session lifetime, and we support immediate session invalidation via our admin console and through SCIM deprovision events; in some cases there is a short token TTL in the service to avoid long-lived tokens.

[05:00] Ethan Park: RBAC — we need least privilege and ability to scope models and routes by team. how granular is that?
[05:08] Rashid Khan: We have role templates (admin, dev, observer) and per-route policies. you can scope access down to model versions and to routes (e.g., embeddings-only vs generation). Dedicated and Private deployments can be configured with additional org-level policies and customer-managed groups brought in via SCIM.
[05:25] Lena Ortiz: do roles map to SAML attributes? we want automated mapping from groups.
[05:30] Marisol Gomez: yes, group->role mapping via SAML assertions or SCIM group sync is supported. mapping config is editable by admins.

[07:00] Jonas Reed: audit logs — we need a canonical log stream for requests/responses, auth events, and admin actions. format JSON ideally, and we'd like exports into our SIEM (Splunk). retention could be 1 year initially, extendable.
[07:12] Alec Moreno: we've got structured audit logs in JSON with request id, user, timestamp, model, tokens generated (count), latency, and a redaction flag. we can ship logs to customer S3, to a streaming destination (kinesis/pubsub), or push via syslog to a collector.
[07:30] Priya Mahajan: what about request/response payloads? we have strict PII rules so we can't send full request bodies into our Splunk.
[07:36] Marisol Gomez: by default payloads are redacted; we provide an audit export schema where payloads are replaced by hashes or redaction markers. customers can opt into fuller logging in Private deployments but there's a compliance review required.

[09:05] Lena Ortiz: KMS and encryption — we have a BYOK policy; keys must be customer-managed and rotate quarterly. support for HSM is required for high-sensitivity models.
[09:16] Rashid Khan: we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault) and we have an HSM-backed option in Private deployments. key rotation is supported; we provide guidance on rolling keys without downtime by using envelope encryption.
[09:35] Ethan Park: so if we bring keys, can you still access token-level telemetry?
[09:40] Marisol Gomez: telemetry like token counts and latency are independent of the data key — we do not hold plaintext customer data encrypted under customer keys; our storage model is envelope-based. with BYOK we never have the plain key. there are limited operational modes where support requires a key escrow under strict controls — but that's exception only.

[11:10] Jonas Reed: For Private vpc deployment — timeline and infra ask. we want a pilot that runs in our VPC with private control plane. what's the typical lead time?
[11:19] Alec Moreno: for a Private deployment pilot it's typically 4–6 weeks to stand up a sandbox in customer's VPC for a small cluster footprint, assuming networking approvals. Dedicated reserved capacity is faster — a week or two if we have the contract and infra slot.
[11:33] Priya Mahajan: what networking requirements? we have limited egress and strict peering rules.
[11:38] Rashid Khan: we'll provide a network requirements doc — we support VPC peering, private link, and restricted egress via NAT. we can also do air-gapped on-prem installs for regulated workloads but that adds time.

[13:00] Lena Ortiz: data retention policy — we need to ensure logs and request traces that we don't want to retain beyond 90 days for prod traffic, though for some workloads we may need 1 year. how flexible are retention windows?
[13:10] Marisol Gomez: retention windows are configurable per tenant in Dedicated and Private. Hosted default is 30 days for payloads and 180 days for metadata; we can provide contractual retention changes for enterprise deals.
[13:22] Ethan Park: and is deletion auditable? we need proof of deletion for certain records.
[13:27] Alec Moreno: yes — deletions produce an audit event and we can provide an export of deletion confirmations for scoped data sets.

[15:00] Jonas Reed: regulatory — do you support data subject requests / right to be forgotten workflows?
[15:07] Marisol Gomez: we have a process: identify tenant data, perform targeted deletion, and provide a compliance report. for Private deployments the customer controls the data store, so they run the process; we provide the tooling.

[17:30] Priya Mahajan: curious about model fallbacks and access controls. if a model is degraded do you route to cheaper variants automatically? we need to ensure routing policies don't leak data across tenants.
[17:40] Rashid Khan: routing policies are tenant-aware; fallbacks route to compatible model variants within the same tenancy and region. we do not route across tenants. for Dedicated instances you can set hard routing policies and disable automatic cross-variant fallbacks.

[19:50] Lena Ortiz: encryption in transit — TLS version and ciphers? we need TLS1.2 minimum and perfect forward secrecy.
[19:56] Marisol Gomez: TLS1.2+ with recommended ciphers and we support TLS1.3. mutual TLS is available for Private and Dedicated control plane connections where customers require mTLS.

[22:00] Ethan Park: incident response and SLAs — what does your incident playbook look like and how are customers notified?
[22:10] Alec Moreno: we maintain an incident response plan and notify via email + status page + optional pager/phone for critical incidents. we have runbooks and post-incident reports for Sev1 incidents. SLAs vary by plan; Dedicated has uptime and latency SLO clauses.

[24:30] Jonas Reed: legal/process question — we often need to recite subprocessor lists and data flow maps. can you provide a current subprocessor list?
[24:38] Marisol Gomez: yes, we maintain a subprocessor list and DPA addendum; we can provide that as a download and sign a DPA for production.

[26:00] Ethan Park: competitive question — how do you compare price/perf vs Bedrock or Anthropic?
[26:08] Alec Moreno: high level — our differentiator is production-first throughput and transparent per-token economics. we provide dedicated pools and private installs which many hosted players don't offer in the same integrated bundle. we'll share benchmark numbers and pricing examples after this call.

[28:40] Priya Mahajan: we want to run a benchmark: 1k concurrent small generation requests, 2048 context, measure p50/p95/p99 latency and token cost. can Redwood run that in our VPC?
[28:52] Rashid Khan: yes — we can run a benchmark. for private pilot we'll do a baseline run in a sandbox VPC with your test data. we'll provide an infra checklist and a runbook.

[31:00] Lena Ortiz: audit log schema — can you share a sample export so our SIEM team can map fields?
[31:06] Marisol Gomez: absolutely — we'll attach a sample audit export (json) and a field mapping doc.

[33:20] Jonas Reed: contractually, we need to include clauses for key ownership and incident notification times. is that acceptable?
[33:27] Alec Moreno: yes — we can include BYOK and incident notification windows in the SOW/contract.

[35:00] Ethan Park: small thing — what's the support model during pilot? SLA? dedicated CSM?
[35:06] Alec Moreno: pilot includes an assigned Solutions Engineer and an AE; dedicated CSM and enterprise support tiers are part of Dedicated/Private commercial terms.

[37:30] Marisol Gomez: I want to call out one constraint: if you opt-in to full request/response logging in Hosted we need an additional compliance review because of PII handling. Private gives you more flexibility.

[39:50] Jonas Reed: understood. what are the typical blockers other customers hit?
[39:55] Rashid Khan: networking approvals and key rotation policies are the top two. also provisioning mapping for very large orgs can take an extra week.

[41:10] Alec Moreno: Recap and next steps — we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts and whitepaper (Alec), Dedicated pricing + SLOs (Marisol), KMS integration guide and audit log schema (Alec), and schedule the benchmark (Rashid + Priya) for the week of 2027-06-28.
[41:35] Lena Ortiz: that works. please mark the items in the ticketing system; we'll review and come back with follow-ups.
[41:44] Priya Mahajan: we'll prepare a small infra sandbox request once we have the runbook.
[41:50] Alec Moreno: great — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with links and a proposed schedule.
[42:10] Jonas Reed: thanks all.
[42:12] Ethan Park: thanks, bye.

Meeting end.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcription of acronyms ("SOC two" for SOC 2, "K M S" spacing), speaker labels may have minor mismatches. There were references to external artifacts: subprocessor_list.pdf (link provided after call), audit_export_sample.json, dedicated-pricing-example.xlsx.

Final recap (auto):
- Interest: Private VPC pilot + Dedicated for prod.
- Must-haves: BYOK + HSM option, SCIM/SAML provisioning, JSON audit exports to SIEM, configurable retention windows, contractual DPA + subprocessor list.
- Gate for pilot: sign NDA/DPA and provide sandbox infra details.

End of transcript.
